    F(T₀) has no summand F(S₋) for T₀ ∈ C #

    The first paragraph of the proof of Theorem 2.7. The manuscript decomposes a finite-dimensional T₁ ⊆ T₀ in C into indecomposables and applies the Krull–Schmidt theorem. We argue with the retractions instead: if P = Φ(S₋) is a summand of Φ(T₁) through an idempotent ε, then ε and Φ(ρ(ε)) agree modulo the nilpotent kernel of ρ, hence are conjugate, so P ≅ Φ(T₁') for the summand T₁' = im ρ(ε) of T₁. Since T₁' ∈ C, it is not isomorphic to S₋, contradicting reflection of isomorphism classes.
